units.zh: 劉皞，字克明，晉丞相譙國公句之弟也。
units.en: Liu Hao, whose courtesy name was Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.
units.literal: Liu Hao, courtesy name Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.

units.zh: 句，《晉書》有傳。
units.en: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.
units.literal: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.

units.zh: 皞少離鄉里，唐天祐中，梁將劉鄩襲太原，軍至樂平，時皞客於縣舍，為鄩軍所俘。
units.en: Hao had left his hometown while still young. During the Tianyou reign of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun attacked Taiyuan; when his army reached Leping, Hao was staying at the county inn and was taken prisoner by Xun's forces.
units.literal: Hao left his native place while still young. In the Tianyou era of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun raided Taiyuan; when the army reached Leping, Hao was lodging at the county guesthouse and was captured by Xun's troops.

units.zh: 謝彥章見之，知其儒者，待之以禮，謂其鄉人劉去非曰：「為君得一宗人。」
units.en: When Xie Yanzhang saw him, he recognized a man of learning and treated him courteously. He told his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."
units.literal: Xie Yanzhang saw him, knew he was a scholar, and treated him with courtesy. He said to his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."

units.zh: 即令皞見之，去非詢其爵裏，乃親族也，對泣久之，自是隨去非客於彥章門下。
units.en: He then had Hao brought to meet him. Qufei inquired into his title and home district and found they were relatives; the two wept together for a long while. Thereafter Hao followed Qufei as a client in Yanzhang's entourage.
units.literal: He then had Hao brought before him. Qufei asked about his rank and native place and found they were kin; the two wept together for a long time. From then on Hao followed Qufei as a guest in Yanzhang's household.

units.zh: 彥章得罪，去非為郢州刺史，皞隨之郡。
units.en: After Yanzhang fell from grace, Qufei was appointed prefect of Yingzhou, and Hao went with him to the prefecture.
units.literal: When Yanzhang fell from favor, Qufei became prefect of Yingzhou, and Hao accompanied him to the prefecture.

units.zh: 莊宗平河洛，去非以嘗從劉守奇歸梁，深懼獲罪，乃棄郡投高季興於荊南，皞累為荊州攝官。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the central plains, Qufei—who had once followed Liu Shouqi in defecting to Liang—feared severe punishment. He abandoned his post and threw in his lot with Gao Jixing in southern Jing; Hao served repeatedly as acting official in Jingzhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the Yellow River region, Qufei, having once followed Liu Shouqi in surrendering to Liang, greatly feared punishment. He abandoned his prefecture and went to Gao Jixing in Jingnan; Hao repeatedly served as acting official in Jingzhou.

units.zh: 既而兄句明宗朝為學士，遣人召歸。
units.en: Later his elder brother Gou became a Hanlin academician under Emperor Mingzong and sent for him to return.
units.literal: Later his elder brother Gou became an academician in the court of Emperor Mingzong and sent someone to summon him home.

units.zh: 梁漢颙鎮鄧州，辟為從事，入為監察御史，歷水部員外郎、史館修撰。
units.en: Liang Hanyong, military governor of Dengzhou, took him on as an aide. He then entered the capital as investigating censor and went on to serve as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
units.literal: Liang Hanyong governed Dengzhou and recruited him as an aide; he entered the capital as investigating censor, then served as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

units.zh: 長興末，宰臣趙鳳鎮邢臺，表為節度判官。
units.en: Near the end of the Changxing era, Chief Minister Zhao Feng was posted to Xingtai and recommended him as adjutant to the military commissioner.
units.literal: At the end of the Changxing era, the chief minister Zhao Feng governed Xingtai and recommended him as military commissioner adjutant.

units.zh: 清泰初，入為起居郎，改駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事，移河南少尹、兵部郎中，轉太府卿。
units.en: Early in the Qingtai era he entered court as recorder of imperial activity, then became vice director of the Transport Ministry while also serving as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business. He was later posted as vice director of Henan, director of the War Ministry, and finally minister of the Grand Treasury.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he entered service as recorder of the emperor's movements, was transferred to vice director of the Transport Ministry, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs. He was moved to vice director of Henan, director of the War Ministry, and then minister of the Grand Treasury.

units.zh: 漢祖受命，用為宗正卿。
units.en: When the founder of Later Han took the throne, he was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.
units.literal: When the Han founder received the mandate, Hao was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.

units.zh: 周初，改衛尉卿。
units.en: Early in the Zhou dynasty he was made minister of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was transferred to minister of the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 廣順元年冬十月，稅居於東京，夜夢鬼詫之曰：「公於我冢上安床，深不奉益。」
units.en: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Guangshun, while renting a house in the Eastern Capital, he dreamed that a ghost rebuked him: "You have set your bed on my grave—this does me no good whatsoever."
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Guangshun, while renting a residence in the Eastern Capital, he dreamed at night that a ghost reproached him, saying, "You have placed your bed on my tomb—this brings me no benefit at all."

units.zh: 皞問鬼姓氏，曰李丕文。
units.en: Hao asked the ghost's surname; it answered, Li Piwen.
units.literal: Hao asked the ghost's surname; it said Li Piwen.

units.zh: 皞曰：「君言殊誤，都城內豈可冢耶？」
units.en: Hao said, "You are quite mistaken—how could there be a grave inside the capital?"
units.literal: Hao said, "What you say is quite mistaken—how could there be a tomb inside the capital city?"

units.zh: 曰：「冢本在野，張十八郎展城時圍入。」
units.en: It replied, "The grave was originally in the countryside; when Zhang the Eighteenth expanded the city walls, it was taken inside."
units.literal: It said, "The tomb was originally in the open country; when Zhang the Eighteenth Son expanded the city, it was enclosed within the walls."

units.zh: 忽寤。
units.en: He woke with a start.
units.literal: He suddenly awoke.

units.zh: 又半月，復夢前鬼曰：「公不相信，屈觀吾舍可乎？」
units.en: Half a month later he dreamed again of the same ghost, who said, "Since you do not believe me, would you do me the honor of visiting my home?"
units.literal: After another half month he again dreamed of the former ghost, who said, "You do not believe me—would you condescend to visit my dwelling?"

units.zh: 即以手掊地，豁然見華第，花木叢萃，房廊雕煥，立皞於西廡。
units.en: It struck the ground with its hand, and at once a splendid mansion appeared—flowers and trees massed together, corridors and halls carved and bright—and it placed Hao in the west wing.
units.literal: It then struck the ground with its hand, and suddenly a splendid mansion appeared, with clustered flowers and trees and carved, gleaming corridors and chambers; it set Hao standing in the west gallery.

units.zh: 久之，見一團火如電，前來漸近，即前鬼也。
units.en: After a long while he saw a ball of fire, swift as lightning, drawing nearer—it was the same ghost as before.
units.literal: After a long while he saw a ball of fire like lightning approaching nearer and nearer—it was the former ghost.

units.zh: 引皞深入，出其孥，泣拜如有所托。
units.en: It led Hao farther inside, brought out its wife and children, and wept and bowed as if placing someone in their care.
units.literal: It led Hao deeper in, brought out its wife and children, and wept and bowed as though entrusting someone with a charge.

units.zh: 皞問丕文鬼事，曰：「冥司各有部屬，外不知也。」
units.en: Hao asked Piwen about the affairs of the netherworld. He replied, "Each office of the underworld has its own staff; outsiders cannot know them."
units.literal: Hao asked Piwen about affairs in the ghost realm. It said, "The underworld offices each have their own subordinates; outsiders cannot know them."

units.zh: 皞曰：「余官何至？」
units.en: Hao asked, "What office will I reach?"
units.literal: Hao said, "What office will I attain?"

units.zh: 再三不對，苦訊之，曰：「齊王判官。」
units.en: It refused to answer despite repeated questioning; only when pressed hard did it say, "Adjutant to the Prince of Qi."
units.literal: It would not answer after repeated questioning; when pressed hard, it said, "Adjutant to the Prince of Qi."

units.zh: 皞曰：「張令公為齊王，去世久矣。
units.en: Hao said, "Lord Zhang was Prince of Qi, and he has been dead for many years.
units.literal: Hao said, "Lord Zhang was Prince of Qi, and he died long ago.

units.zh: 今鄆州高令公為齊王，余方為列卿，豈復為賓佐乎？」
units.en: Now Lord Gao of Yanzhou is Prince of Qi, and I am already a chief minister of a department—how could I become someone's staff officer again?"
units.literal: Now Lord Gao of Yanzhou is Prince of Qi, and I am presently a chief minister of a department—how could I again become a client's aide?"

units.zh: 鬼曰：「不知也。」
units.en: The ghost said, "I do not know."
units.literal: The ghost said, "I do not know."

units.zh: 皞既寤，欲掘而視之。
units.en: When Hao woke, he wanted to dig and see for himself.
units.literal: When Hao awoke, he wished to dig and see for himself.

units.zh: 既而又告人曰：「鬼雖見訴，其如吾稅舍何？」
units.en: But then he told someone, "The ghost may have complained, but what can I do about the house I am renting?"
units.literal: Yet he then told someone, "Though the ghost has appealed to me, what am I to do about my rented house?"

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: So he let the matter drop.
units.literal: and so he stopped.

units.zh: 廣順二年春，朝廷以皞為高麗冊使。
units.en: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, the court appointed Hao envoy to invest the king of Goryeo.
units.literal: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, the court appointed Hao envoy to invest the king of Goryeo.

units.zh: 三月，至鄆，節度使高行周以皞嗜酒，留連累日，旦夕沈醉。
units.en: In the third month he reached Yan. Military Governor Gao Xingzhou, knowing Hao's love of drink, kept him for many days, and from morning to night he was deep in his cups.
units.literal: In the third month he reached Yan; the military governor Gao Xingzhou, knowing Hao's fondness for wine, detained him for many days, and morning and evening he drank to drunkenness.

units.zh: 其月二十三日，晨興櫛發，狀如醉寐，男泳視之，已卒矣。
units.en: On the twenty-third of that month, as he rose in the morning to comb his hair, he appeared drunk and drowsy; his son Yong looked in on him and found he was already dead.
units.literal: On the twenty-third day of that month, as he rose in the morning to comb his hair, he seemed drunk and asleep; his son Yong looked at him and found he had already died.

units.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》云：銜命使吳越，路由鄆州，卒於郵亭。）〉
units.en: (According to the 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》: While bearing imperial orders to Wu and Yue, he passed through Yanzhou on the route and died at a courier station.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》 says: While on a mission to Wu and Yue, he passed through Yanzhou on the way and died at a post station.)〉

units.zh: 時年六十一。
units.en: He was sixty-one years old at the time.
units.literal: He was sixty-one at the time.

units.zh: 其年八月，鄆帥齊王高行周亦夢鬼請齊王判官，得無是乎！
units.en: In the eighth month of that year, Gao Xingzhou, Prince of Qi and governor of Yan, likewise dreamed that a ghost was seeking an adjutant to the Prince of Qi—surely this was no coincidence!
units.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Gao Xingzhou, Prince of Qi and military governor of Yan, also dreamed that a ghost requested an adjutant to the Prince of Qi—could this not have been the same affair!

units.zh: 皞從儒學，好聚書，嗜酒無儀檢，然衷抱無他，急於行義，士友以此多之。
units.en: Hao had pursued Confucian studies, loved to collect books, and was devoted to wine and lax in propriety; yet he harbored no ulterior motives and was quick to act on principle, which is why men of learning esteemed him.
units.literal: Hao followed Confucian learning, loved to collect books, and was fond of wine and careless in deportment; yet in his inner mind he harbored no other designs and was eager in righteous conduct, for which scholar-friends held him in high regard.

units.zh: 張沆，字太元，徐州人。
units.en: Zhang Hang, whose courtesy name was Taiyuan, came from Xuzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Hang, courtesy name Taiyuan, was a native of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 父嚴，本州牙將。
units.en: His father Yan was a military adjutant in the prefecture.
units.literal: His father Yan was a military adjutant of the prefecture.

units.zh: 沆少力學，攻詞賦，登進士第。
units.en: In his youth Hang studied diligently, excelled in rhapsodies and fu, and passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: Hang in youth applied himself to study, specialized in rhapsodies and fu, and passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 唐明宗子秦王好文，然童年疏率，動不由禮。
units.en: The Prince of Qin, a son of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, loved literature, but as a youth he was careless and impulsive and seldom observed propriety.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin, son of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, loved literature, but in his youth he was careless and unrestrained, and his actions did not follow ritual.

units.zh: 每賓僚大集，手自出題，令面前賦詩，少不如意，則壞裂抵棄。
units.en: Whenever he gathered his guests and staff in large numbers, he would set topics himself and demand impromptu poems; if a composition fell even slightly short, he would tear it up and throw it away.
units.literal: Whenever his guests and staff assembled in great numbers, he would personally set topics and order those before him to compose poems on the spot; if the result was the least unsatisfactory, he would tear it up and cast it aside.

units.zh: 沆初以刺謁，秦王屬合座客各為《南湖廳記》，因謂沆曰：「聞生名久矣，請為此文。」
units.en: When Hang first presented his visiting card, the Prince of Qin asked every guest present to compose a 《Record of the South Lake Hall》, and said to Hang, "I have heard your name for a long time—please write this essay."
units.literal: When Hang first called on him with a visiting card, the Prince of Qin assigned all the guests at the gathering to compose a 《Record of the South Lake Hall》, and said to Hang, "I have long heard your name—please write this piece."

units.zh: 沆不獲已，從之。
units.en: Hang, unable to decline, complied.
units.literal: Hang, unable to refuse, complied.

units.zh: 及群士記成，獨取沆所為勒之於石，繇是署為河南府巡官。
units.en: When the scholars had all finished, he chose only Hang's piece to be carved in stone; Hang was then appointed touring official of the Henan prefectural government.
units.literal: When the scholars' compositions were finished, he alone took Hang's work and had it carved on stone; thereby Hang was appointed touring official of Henan prefecture.

units.zh: 秦王敗，勒歸鄉里。
units.en: After the Prince of Qin's downfall, Hang was forced to return home.
units.literal: When the Prince of Qin was defeated, Hang was compelled to return to his native place.

units.zh: 晉初，桑維翰秉政，沆以文幹進，用為著作佐郎、集賢校理，遷右拾遺。
units.en: Early in Jin, when Sang Weihan held power, Hang rose on his literary ability and was appointed assistant compiler and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then promoted to right remembrancer.
units.literal: Early in Jin, Sang Weihan held power; Hang advanced on the strength of his literary talent and was appointed assistant compiler and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then promoted to right remembrancer.

units.zh: 維翰出鎮，奏為記室。
units.en: When Weihan took up a provincial command, he recommended Hang as recorder on his staff.
units.literal: When Weihan went out to govern a circuit, he memorialized to have Hang made recorder in his staff.

units.zh: 從維翰入朝，授殿中侍御史。
units.en: When Weihan returned to court, Hang was appointed palace attendant censor.
units.literal: Following Weihan to court, he was appointed palace attendant censor.

units.zh: 歲餘，自侍御史改祠部員外郎知制誥，召入翰林為學士。
units.en: After a little more than a year he moved from attendant censor to vice director of the Rites Ministry with responsibility for drafting edicts, and was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred from attendant censor to vice director of the Rites Ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and was summoned into the Hanlin as academician.

units.zh: 維翰罷相，馮玉用事，不欲沆居禁密，改右諫議大夫，罷其職。
units.en: After Weihan left the chief ministership, Feng Yu took power and did not want Hang in the inner secretariat; Hang was made right admonishing grandee and relieved of his Hanlin post.
units.literal: When Weihan was removed as chief minister, Feng Yu came to power and did not wish Hang to remain in the inner secretariat; he was made right admonishing grandee and dismissed from that office.

units.zh: 漢祖至汴，轉右常侍，復用為學士，未幾，遷工部尚書充職。
units.en: When the founder of Later Han reached Bian, Hang became right attendant at court and was again made a Hanlin academician; soon afterward he was promoted to minister of Works while keeping the academician post.
units.literal: When the Han founder reached Bian, Hang was transferred to right attendant at court and again appointed academician; before long he was promoted to minister of Works while retaining the post.

units.zh: 明年，以營奉葬事求解職，改禮部尚書。
units.en: The following year he asked to be relieved of duty in order to oversee funeral arrangements and was made minister of Rites.
units.literal: The next year, on grounds of arranging funeral observances, he requested leave from his post and was made minister of Rites.

units.zh: 及歸朝，復為學士。
units.en: When he returned to court, he was again made a Hanlin academician.
units.literal: When he returned to court, he again became academician.

units.zh: 太祖以沆耳疾罷職，改刑部尚書。
units.en: Because of Hang's ear ailment, Emperor Taizu relieved him of the Hanlin post and appointed him minister of Justice.
units.literal: Because of Hang's ear ailment, Emperor Taizu removed him from the post and made him minister of Justice.

units.zh: 廣順二年秋，命為故齊王高行周冊贈使，復命而卒。
units.en: In the autumn of the second year of Guangshun he was appointed envoy to confer posthumous honors on the late Prince of Qi, Gao Xingzhou; he died upon returning from the mission.
units.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Guangshun he was ordered to serve as envoy to confer posthumous honors on the late Prince of Qi, Gao Xingzhou; he returned from the mission and died.

units.zh: 贈太子少保。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 沆性儒雅，好釋氏，雖久居祿位，家無餘財，死之日，圖書之外，唯使鄆之資耳。
units.en: Hang was refined and scholarly and fond of Buddhism. Though he had long held office, his household had no surplus wealth; when he died, aside from his books, he possessed only the travel funds for his mission to Yan.
units.literal: Hang's nature was refined and scholarly; he loved Buddhism. Though he long held salaried office, his household had no surplus wealth; on the day of his death, apart from books, he had only the funds for his mission to Yan.

units.zh: 嗣子尚幼，親友慮其耗散，上言於太祖，乃令三司差人主葬，余資市邸舍，以贍其孤焉。
units.en: His heir was still a child; relatives and friends, fearing the estate would be squandered, appealed to Emperor Taizu, who ordered the Three Departments to arrange the funeral; the remaining funds were used to buy a shop-house to support the orphan.
units.literal: His heir was still young; relatives and friends feared the estate would be dissipated and memorialized Emperor Taizu, who then ordered the Three Departments to assign someone to oversee the funeral; the remaining funds were used to purchase a shop residence to support the orphan.

units.zh: 沆記覽文史，好征求僻事，公家應用，時出一聯以炫奇筆，故不為馮玉所重。
units.en: Hang was widely read in literature and history and delighted in obscure lore; in official documents he would sometimes insert a striking couplet to show off his wit, which is why Feng Yu did not esteem him.
units.literal: Hang was well read in literature and history and loved to seek out obscure facts; in official documents he would sometimes produce a couplet to display his unusual pen, and therefore was not highly regarded by Feng Yu.

units.zh: 雖有聵疾，猶出入金門，凡五六年。
units.en: Despite his deafness, he continued to attend court at the Golden Gate for five or six years.
units.literal: Though he had deafness, he still went in and out of the Golden Gate for some five or six years.

units.zh: 漢隱帝末年，楊、史遇害，翌日，沆方知之，聽猶未審，忽問同僚曰：「竊聞盜殺史公，其盜獲否？」
units.en: In the last years of Emperor Yindi of Han, Yang and Shi were murdered; Hang learned of it only the next day. His hearing was still poor, and he suddenly asked a colleague, "I hear bandits killed Lord Shi—have the bandits been caught?"
units.literal: In the last years of Emperor Yindi of Han, Yang and Shi were killed; the next day Hang only then learned of it. His hearing was still unclear, and he suddenly asked a colleague, "I have heard in private that bandits killed Lord Shi—have the bandits been captured?"

units.zh: 是時京師恟懼之次，聞者笑之。
units.en: At a time when the capital was gripped by panic, those who heard him laughed.
units.literal: At that time the capital was in the midst of alarm and fear; those who heard laughed.

units.zh: 有士人申光遜者，與沆友善，沆未病時，夢沆手出小佛塔示光遜，視其上有詩十四字云：「今生不見故人面，明月高高上翠樓。」
units.en: A scholar named Shen Guangxun was friendly with Hang. Before Hang fell ill, Guangxun dreamed that Hang held out a small Buddhist pagoda for him to see; on it was a fourteen-character poem: "In this life I shall not see an old friend's face; the bright moon climbs high above the green tower."
units.literal: There was a scholar named Shen Guangxun who was on friendly terms with Hang. Before Hang fell ill, Guangxun dreamed that Hang took out a small Buddhist pagoda from his hand and showed it to him; looking at it, he saw a poem of fourteen characters: "In this life I shall not see an old friend's face; the bright moon climbs high above the green tower."

units.zh: 光遜既寤，心惡之，俄聞沆卒。
units.en: When Guangxun woke, he was troubled by the dream; before long he heard that Hang had died.
units.literal: When Guangxun awoke, his heart took it ill; soon he heard that Hang had died.

units.zh: 張可復，字伯恭，德州平原人也。
units.en: Zhang Kefu, whose courtesy name was Bogong, came from Pingyuan in Dezhou.
units.literal: Zhang Kefu, courtesy name Bogong, was a native of Pingyuan in Dezhou.

units.zh: 父達，累贈戶部侍郎。
units.en: His father Da was repeatedly granted posthumous promotion to vice minister of the Household Ministry.
units.literal: His father Da was posthumously enfeoffed repeatedly as vice minister of the Household Ministry.

units.zh: 可復略通儒術，少習吏事。
units.en: Kefu had a modest grounding in Confucian learning and trained in clerical work from youth.
units.literal: Kefu had some knowledge of Confucian learning and in youth practiced clerical affairs.

units.zh: 梁末，薄遊於魏，鄴王羅紹威表為安陽簿。
units.en: Late in Liang he traveled in Wei; the Prince of Ye, Luo Shaowei, recommended him as recorder of Anyang.
units.literal: At the end of Liang he traveled lightly in Wei; the Prince of Ye, Luo Shaowei, memorialized to appoint him recorder of Anyang.

units.zh: 唐天成初，依晉公霍彥威於青州，為從事。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era of Tang he joined Duke Jin Huo Yanwei in Qingzhou as an aide.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng in Tang he attached himself to Duke Jin Huo Yanwei in Qingzhou and served as an aide.

units.zh: 晉公以其滑稽好避事，目為「奸兔兒」。
units.en: The duke, finding him witty and prone to dodge responsibility, nicknamed him "the crafty little rabbit."
units.literal: The duke, because he was witty and fond of shirking duties, called him "the crafty little rabbit."

units.zh: 長興中入朝，拜監察御史，六遷至兵部郎中，賜金紫。
units.en: During the Changxing era he entered court as investigating censor; after six promotions he became director of the War Ministry and was awarded the gold-and-purple insignia.
units.literal: During Changxing he entered court and was appointed investigating censor; after six promotions he reached director of the War Ministry and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

units.zh: 晉天福中，自西京留守判官入為秘書少監，改左司郎中。
units.en: During the Tianfu era of Jin he moved from adjutant to the western capital's military governor to vice director of the Secretariat in the capital, then became director of the left bureau.
units.literal: During Tianfu in Jin he went from adjutant to the western capital's military governor into the capital as vice director of the Secretariat, then was made director of the left bureau.

units.zh: 開運中，遷左諫議大夫。
units.en: During the Kaiyun era he was promoted to left admonishing grandee.
units.literal: During Kaiyun he was promoted to left admonishing grandee.

units.zh: 漢乾祐初，湘陰公鎮徐方，朝行中選可以從戎者，因授武寧軍節度副使、檢校禮部尚書。
units.en: Early in the Qianyou era of Han, when the Duke of Xiangyin governed Xuzhou, the court selected an official fit for military service and appointed Kefu vice military commissioner of Wuning and acting minister of Rites.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou in Han, the Duke of Xiangyin governed Xuzhou; among court officials one able to follow the army was chosen, and Kefu was appointed vice military commissioner of the Wuning army and acting minister of Rites.

units.zh: 及世宗鎮澶淵，改鎮寧軍節度行軍司馬。
units.en: When the future Emperor Shizong was posted to Chanzhou, Kefu became campaigning marshal of the Zhenning circuit.
units.literal: When Emperor Shizong governed Chanzhou, Kefu was made campaigning marshal of the Zhenning circuit.

units.zh: 三年，征拜給事中。
units.en: In the third year he was summoned to court as attendant gentleman.
units.literal: In the third year he was summoned and appointed attendant gentleman.

units.zh: 世宗嗣位，以澶淵幕府之舊，拜右散騎常侍。
units.en: When Shizong took the throne, in recognition of their earlier service together at Chanzhou he was made right regular attendant at court.
units.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, on account of their old ties in the Chanzhou staff he was appointed right regular attendant at court.

units.zh: 顯德元年秋，以疾卒，年七十有三。
units.en: In the autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness at the age of seventy-three.
units.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness at the age of seventy-three.

units.zh: 制贈戶部尚書。
units.en: An edict posthumously granted him the title minister of the Household Ministry.
units.literal: By imperial order he was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of the Household Ministry.

units.zh: 可復無他才，惟以謹願保長年，加之迂懦，多為同列輕俊者所侮，而累階至金紫，居三品之秩，亦其命耶！
units.en: Kefu had no special talent; he relied only on cautious docility to prolong his years, and being besides pedantic and timid, he was often mocked by cleverer colleagues—yet he climbed step by step to gold-and-purple and third-rank office: was this not simply his destiny!
units.literal: Kefu had no other talent; he relied solely on cautious willingness to preserve long life, and moreover was pedantic and timid, and was often insulted by light-minded colleagues—yet he rose step by step to gold-and-purple and held rank of the third grade: was this not his fate!

units.zh: 於德辰，字進明，元城人也。
units.en: Yu Dechen, whose courtesy name was Jinming, came from Yuancheng.
units.literal: Yu Dechen, courtesy name Jinming, was a native of Yuancheng.

units.zh: 幼敏悟，篤誌好學，及射策文場，數上不調。
units.en: As a boy he was bright and quick, devoted to study; yet when he took the civil examinations he failed again and again.
units.literal: In youth he was keen and perceptive, devoted in will and fond of learning; when he competed in the examination hall, he repeatedly failed to pass.

units.zh: 後唐明宗鎮邢州，德辰往謁焉，明宗見而器之，因得假官於屬邑。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang was posted to Xingzhou, Dechen went to see him; Mingzong took a liking to him and secured him a provisional post in a county under the prefecture.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang governed Xingzhou, Dechen went to call on him; Mingzong saw him and valued him, and he thereby obtained a provisional post in a subordinate county.

units.zh: 後繼歷州縣，歷仕晉、漢、周，官至工部尚書。
units.en: He later served in successive county and prefectural posts, held office under Jin, Han, and Zhou, and rose to minister of Works.
units.literal: He later successively served in prefectures and counties, held office through Jin, Han, and Zhou, and reached the post of minister of Works.

units.zh: 王延，字世美，鄚州長豐人也。
units.en: Wang Yan, whose courtesy name was Shimei, came from Changfeng in Mozhou.
units.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shimei, was a native of Changfeng in Mozhou.

units.zh: 少為儒，善詞賦，會鄉曲離亂，不獲從鄉薦，因客於浮陽，隨滄帥戴思遠入梁。
units.en: In youth he studied the classics and excelled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home region fell into chaos he could not obtain a local recommendation, so he lodged in Fuyang and followed the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang service.
units.literal: In youth he was a Confucian scholar, skilled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home district was torn by disorder he could not obtain local recommendation, and therefore lodged in Fuyang, following the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang.

units.zh: 嘗以所為賦謁梁相李琪，琪覽之，欣然曰：「此道近難其人，王生升我堂矣。」
units.en: He once presented a fu he had written to Liang Chancellor Li Qi, who read it and said with delight, "This art has lately lacked a true master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my level."
units.literal: He once presented a fu he had written to the Liang chancellor Li Qi; Qi read it and said with pleasure, "In recent times this art has lacked its master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my hall."

units.zh: 繇是人士稱之。
units.en: From that time men of letters spoke highly of him.
units.literal: From this men of letters praised him.

units.zh: 尋薦為即墨縣令，歷徐、宋、鄆、青四鎮從事。
units.en: He was soon recommended as magistrate of Jimo and went on to serve as aide in the Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing circuits.
units.literal: Soon he was recommended as magistrate of Jimo and successively served as aide in the four circuits of Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing.

units.zh: 長興初，鄉人馮道、趙鳳在相位，擢拜左補闕。
units.en: Early in the Changxing era his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were chief ministers; he was promoted to left supplementer.
units.literal: At the beginning of Changxing his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng held the chief ministership; he was promoted and appointed left supplementer.

units.zh: 逾年，以水部員外知制誥遷中書舍人，賜金紫。
units.en: A year later he moved from vice director of the Water Ministry with responsibility for drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and received the gold-and-purple insignia.
units.literal: After a year he was transferred from vice director of the Water Ministry with charge of drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and was granted gold-and-purple.

units.zh: 清泰末，以本官權知貢舉。
units.en: Near the end of the Qingtai era he was appointed in his existing post to oversee the civil examinations.
units.literal: At the end of Qingtai he was appointed in his existing office to act as director of the civil examinations.

units.zh: 時有舉子崔頎者，故相協之子也。
units.en: Among the candidates was Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.
units.literal: At the time there was an examinee named Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.

units.zh: 協素與吏部尚書盧文紀不睦，及延將入貢院，文紀謂延曰：「舍人以謹重聞於時，所以去冬老夫在相位時，與諸相首以長者聞奏，用掌文衡。
units.en: Xie had long been at odds with Minister of Personnel Lu Wenji. As Yan was about to enter the examination hall, Wenji told him, "You are known for your caution and gravity; that is why last winter, when I was chief minister, I was the first among the ministers to recommend a man of mature reputation to oversee the examinations.
units.literal: Xie had long been on bad terms with the minister of Personnel Lu Wenji; as Yan was about to enter the examination compound, Wenji said to him, "You, Drafter, are known in the age for caution and weight; therefore last winter, when this old man was chief minister, I reported first among the ministers that a man of mature reputation should be appointed to hold the literary scales.

units.zh: 然貢闈取士，頗多面目。
units.en: Yet in selecting candidates for the examinations, personal connections often play a large part.
units.literal: Yet in selecting scholars in the examination compound, there are often many personal connections.

units.zh: 說者云：『越人善泅，生子方晬，乳母浮之水上。
units.en: As the saying goes: "The people of Yue are skilled swimmers; when a child is barely a month old, the wet nurse floats him on the water."
units.literal: Storytellers say: "The people of Yue are skilled at swimming; when a child is just one month old, the wet nurse floats him on the water."

units.zh: 或駭然止之，乳母曰，其父善泅，子必無溺。』
units.en: Someone alarmed tries to stop her; the wet nurse says, "His father is a skilled swimmer—the child will surely not drown."
units.literal: Someone in alarm tries to stop it; the wet nurse says, "His father is skilled at swimming—the child will surely not drown."

units.zh: 今若以名下取士，即此類也。
units.en: If you choose candidates today by family name and reputation alone, it is exactly this sort of thing.
units.literal: If today one selects scholars by name, it is just this sort of thing.

units.zh: 舍人當求實才，以副公望。」
units.en: You, as Drafter, should seek genuine talent to live up to the reputation you enjoy."
units.literal: You, Drafter, ought to seek real talent, to fulfill public expectation.

units.zh: 延退而謂人曰：「盧公之言，蓋為崔頎也。
units.en: Yan withdrew and told others, "Master Lu's remarks were surely directed at Cui Qi.
units.literal: Yan withdrew and said to others, "Master Lu's words were surely aimed at Cui Qi.

units.zh: 縱與其父不悅，致意何至此耶！」
units.en: Even if he bore ill will toward the boy's father, why make his meaning so plain!"
units.literal: Even if he was displeased with the man's father, why carry the hint to such an extent!

units.zh: 來春，以頎登甲科。
units.en: The next spring, Cui Qi placed in the highest tier of the examinations.
units.literal: The following spring, Hao passed in the top tier of the examinations.

units.zh: 其年，改御史中丞，歲滿，轉尚書右丞。
units.en: That same year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, and when his term ended he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.
units.literal: That year he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.

units.zh: 奉使兩浙，吳人深重之。
units.en: While serving as envoy to the Two Zhes, he won the deep respect of the people of Wu.
units.literal: On a mission to the Two Zhes, the people of Wu held him in deep esteem.

units.zh: 復命，授吏部侍郎，改尚書左丞，拜太常卿，歷工、禮、刑三尚書。
units.en: After reporting back, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and went on to hold the ministries of Works, Rites, and Punishments in succession.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and served successively as Minister of Works, Rites, and Punishments.

units.zh: 以疾求分司西洛，授太子少保。
units.en: He pleaded illness and asked for a post in the Luoyang branch office in the west, and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: Citing illness, he requested a post in the western Luoyang branch office and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 既而連月請告，為留臺所糾，改少傅致仕。
units.en: Before long he took medical leave month after month, was censured by the Luoyang branch office, and was reassigned as Junior Preceptor before retiring from office.
units.literal: Soon afterward he repeatedly took leave for months on end and was censured by the Luoyang branch office; he was changed to Junior Preceptor and retired.

units.zh: 廣順二年冬卒，時年七十有三。
units.en: He died in the winter of the second year of Guangshun, at the age of seventy-three.
units.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged seventy-three.

units.zh: 子億，仕皇朝為殿中丞。
units.en: His son Yi served the present dynasty as a Director in the Palace Bureau.
units.literal: His son Yi served the present dynasty as Director in the Palace Bureau.

units.zh: 申文炳，字國華，洛陽人也。
units.en: Shen Wenbing, whose courtesy name was Guohua, was a native of Luoyang.
units.literal: Shen Wenbing, courtesy name Guohua, was a native of Luoyang.

units.zh: 父鄂，唐左千牛衛將軍。
units.en: His father E had been Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard under the Tang.
units.literal: His father E was Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard under Tang.

units.zh: 文炳長興中進士擢第，釋褐中正軍節度推官，歷孟、懷支使，鄆城、陜縣二邑宰，自澶州觀察判官入為右補闕。
units.en: Wenbing passed the jinshi examination in the Changxing era and began his career as administrative aide to the military governor of Zhongzheng Army. He later served as branch commissioner in Meng and Huai, as magistrate of Yuncheng and Shaan County, and entered court from his post as administrative aide to the Cizhou governor, becoming Right Remonstrance Officer.
units.literal: Wenbing passed the jinshi examination in the Changxing era, took his first office as administrative aide to the military governor of Zhongzheng Army, served successively as branch commissioner of Meng and Huai, magistrate of the two districts of Yuncheng and Shaan County, and entered court from his post as administrative aide to the governor of Cizhou, becoming Right Remonstrance Officer.

units.zh: 晉開運初，授虞部員外知制誥，轉金部郎中充職。
units.en: At the start of the Kaiyun era of Jin he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works with concurrent duty drafting edicts, then transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue in the same capacity.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyun era of Jin he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works with concurrent duty as drafter of edicts, then transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue to fill that post.

units.zh: 廣順中，為學士，遷中書舍人、知貢舉。
units.en: During the Guangshun era he became an Academician, then was promoted to Drafter in the Secretariat and put in charge of the civil examinations.
units.literal: In the Guangshun era he became an Academician, then was promoted to Drafter in the Secretariat and director of the civil examinations.

units.zh: 〈（《玉壺清話》：李慶，顯德中舉進士，工詩，有云：「醉輕浮世事，老重故鄉人。」
units.en: (From 《Jade Pot Pure Talk》: Li Qing passed the jinshi examination in the Xiande era and was skilled at poetry. One of his lines runs, "Drunk, I lightly float past worldly affairs; in old age I deeply cherish the people of my homeland."
units.literal: (《Jade Pot Pure Talk》: Li Qing passed the jinshi examination in the Xiande era and was skilled at poetry. He wrote, "Drunk, I lightly float past the affairs of the world; old, I deeply cherish the people of my homeland."

units.zh: 樞密王樸以此一聯薦於申文炳。
units.en: Wang Pu, Commissioner of Military Affairs, recommended this couplet to Shen Wenbing.
units.literal: The Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu recommended this couplet to Shen Wenbing.

units.zh: 文炳知貢舉，遂為第三人。）〉
units.en: When Wenbing oversaw the examinations, he placed Li third overall.)〉
units.literal: Wenbing, as director of the examinations, then placed him third.)〉

units.zh: 顯德五年秋，以疾解職，授左散騎常侍。
units.en: In the autumn of the fifth year of Xiande he resigned because of illness and was appointed Left Regular Attendant.
units.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Xiande he resigned his post because of illness and was appointed Left Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 六年秋，卒於家，時年五十。
units.en: In the autumn of the sixth year he died at home, at the age of fifty.
units.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he died at home, aged fifty.

units.zh: 文炳為文典雅，有訓誥之風。
units.en: Wenbing wrote in an elegant style with the dignified tone of imperial edicts and admonitions.
units.literal: Wenbing's writing was refined and elegant, with the tone of imperial instructions.

units.zh: 執性紓緩，待搢紳以禮，中年而卒，皆惜之。
units.en: He was gentle and unhurried by nature and treated the gentry with courtesy. He died in midlife, and all who knew him mourned the loss.
units.literal: His disposition was gentle and unhurried, and he treated the gentry with courtesy; he died in midlife, and all regretted it.

units.zh: 扈載，少好學，善屬文，賦頌碑贊尤其所長。
units.en: Hu Zai loved learning from youth and was skilled at literary composition, especially rhapsodies, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and encomia.
units.literal: Hu Zai from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; rhapsodies, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and encomia were his particular strengths.

units.zh: 廣順初，隨計於禮部，文價為一時之最，是歲升高等。
units.en: At the start of Guangshun he traveled to the Ministry of Rites for the examinations. His literary reputation was the finest of the day, and that year he placed in the highest tier.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he went up to the Ministry of Rites for the examinations; the market value of his writing was the highest of the age, and that year he was placed in the top tier.

units.zh: 載因遊相國寺，見庭竹可愛，作《碧鮮賦》題其壁。
units.en: While visiting Xiangguo Temple, Zai saw the courtyard bamboo and was charmed by it, so he wrote 《Rhapsody on Emerald Freshness》 on the temple wall.
units.literal: Zai happened to visit Xiangguo Temple, saw the courtyard bamboo and found it delightful, and wrote 《Rhapsody on Emerald Freshness》 on its wall.

units.zh: 世宗聞之，遣小黃門就壁錄之，覽而稱善，因拜水部員外郎知制誥，遷翰林學士，賜緋。
units.en: When Shizong heard of it, he sent a palace attendant to copy the text from the wall. After reading it and praising it, he appointed Zai Vice Director in the Ministry of Works with duty drafting edicts, promoted him to Hanlin Academician, and granted him the scarlet robe.
units.literal: Shizong heard of it, sent a palace attendant to copy it from the wall, read it and praised it, and thereupon appointed him Vice Director in the Ministry of Works with duty drafting edicts, promoted him to Hanlin Academician, and bestowed the scarlet robe.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·李蒨傳》：扈載以文章馳名，樞密使王樸薦令知制誥，除書未下，樸詣中書言之，蒨曰：「斯人命薄，慮不克享耳。」
units.en: (From 《History of Song · Biography of Li Qian》: Hu Zai was renowned for his writing. Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu recommended him to draft edicts. Before the appointment decree was issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to discuss the matter, and Qian said, "This man's fate is thin—I fear he will not live long enough to enjoy the appointment."
units.literal: (《History of Song · Biography of Li Qian》: Hu Zai was famed for his literary writing. The Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Pu recommended him to draft edicts; before the appointment decree was issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to speak of it, and Qian said, "This man's fate is thin—I fear he will not live to enjoy the post."

units.zh: 樸曰：「公在衡石之地，當以材進人，何得言命而遺才。」
units.en: Pu replied, "You stand where the scales of office are held; you should advance men for their talent. How can you speak of fate and leave talent unused?"
units.literal: Pu said, "You stand in the place of the balance and weight; you ought to advance men by talent—how can you speak of fate and leave talent unused?"

units.zh: 載遂知制誥、遷翰林學士，未幾卒。
units.en: Zai was then appointed to draft edicts and promoted to Hanlin Academician, but before long he died.
units.literal: Zai then received the post drafting edicts and was promoted to Hanlin Academician, and before long he died.

units.zh: 世謂樸能薦士，蒨能知人。）〉
units.en: People of the time said that Pu knew how to recommend talent and Qian knew how to read men.)〉
units.literal: The age said that Pu could recommend scholars and Qian could discern men.)〉

units.zh: 而載已病，不能謝，居百餘日，乃力疾入直學士院。
units.en: By then Zai was already ill and could not go to offer thanks. After more than a hundred days at home, he forced himself, despite his illness, to report for duty at the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: But Zai was already ill and could not go to offer thanks; after more than a hundred days at home, he forced himself, though sick, to enter duty at the Academy.

units.zh: 世宗憐之，賜誥還第，遣太醫視疾。
units.en: Shizong took pity on him, granted him the appointment decree and sent him home, and dispatched the imperial physician to attend him.
units.literal: Shizong took pity on him, granted him the appointment decree and sent him home, and dispatched the imperial physician to treat his illness.

units.zh: 年三十有六卒。
units.en: He died at the age of thirty-six.
units.literal: He died at the age of thirty-six.

units.zh: 載始自解褐至終才四年，而與劉袞皆有才無命，時論惜之。
units.en: From the time Zai first took office until his death was only four years. Both he and Liu Gun were men of talent cut short by fate, and public opinion mourned the loss.
units.literal: From Zai's first office to his end was only four years, and both he and Liu Gun had talent but not fate; opinion of the time regretted it.

units.zh: 劉袞，彭城人。
units.en: Liu Gun was a native of Pengcheng.
units.literal: Liu Gun was a native of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 神爽氣俊，富有文藻，繇進士第任左拾遺，與扈載齊名，年二十八而卒。
units.en: Bright of spirit and lofty in bearing, he was richly gifted in letters. After passing the jinshi examination he was appointed Left Reminder, won fame equal to Hu Zai's, and died at the age of twenty-eight.
units.literal: His spirit was bright and his bearing lofty; he was rich in literary ornament. Through the jinshi degree he was appointed Left Reminder, was as famed as Hu Zai, and died at twenty-eight.

units.zh: 賈緯，真定獲鹿人也。
units.en: Jia Wei was a native of Huolu in Zhending.
units.literal: Jia Wei was a native of Huolu in Zhending.

units.zh: 〈（宋祁《景文集·賈令君墓誌銘》：賈氏自唐司空魏國公耽，世貫滄州南皮，子孫稍稍徙真定。
units.en: (From Song Qi's 《Collected Works of Jing · Epitaph for Lord Jia》: The Jia clan traced its line to Tang Minister of Works and Duke of Wei Dan, who had long been established in Nanpi in Cangzhou; the descendants gradually moved to Zhending.
units.literal: (Song Qi's 《Collected Works of Jing · Epitaph for Lord Jia》: The Jia clan, from Tang Minister of Works and Duke of Wei Dan, had long been established in Nanpi in Cangzhou, and the descendants gradually moved to Zhending.

units.zh: 五世祖諒，高祖瑾。
units.en: His fifth-generation ancestor was Liang, and his great-grandfather was Jin.
units.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Liang; his great-grandfather was Jin.

units.zh: 曾祖處士諱初，有至性，疾世方亂，守鄉里，不肯事四方。
units.en: His great-grandfather, the retired gentleman whose taboo name was Chu, was a man of deep sincerity. Distressed by the disorder of the age, he remained in his home district and refused to serve elsewhere.
units.literal: His great-grandfather, the retired gentleman whose taboo name was Chu, had utmost sincerity of nature; sick at the disorder of the age, he kept to his home district and would not serve in any quarter.

units.zh: 祖諱緯。）〉
units.en: His grandfather's taboo name was Wei.)〉
units.literal: His grandfather's taboo name was Wei.)〉

units.zh: 少苦學為文，唐末舉進士不第，遇亂歸河朔，本府累署參軍、邑宰。
units.en: In youth he studied writing with great effort. At the end of the Tang he failed the jinshi examination, and when chaos broke out he returned to the north of the Yellow River, where the local prefecture repeatedly appointed him as aide and district magistrate.
units.literal: In youth he studied writing with hardship; at the end of Tang he failed the jinshi examination, and when disorder came he returned to the north of the Yellow River, where the local prefecture repeatedly appointed him as aide and district magistrate.

units.zh: 唐天成中，範延光鎮定州，表授趙州軍事判官，遷石邑縣令。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era of Tang, when Fan Yanguang governed Dingzhou, he recommended Wei for appointment as military administrative aide of Zhao Prefecture, and Wei was later promoted to magistrate of Shiyi County.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang, when Fan Yanguang governed Dingzhou, he memorialized to appoint Wei military administrative aide of Zhao Prefecture, and Wei was later promoted to magistrate of Shiyi County.

units.zh: 緯屬文之外，勤於撰述，以唐代諸帝實錄，自武宗已下闕而不紀，乃采掇近代傳聞之事，及諸家小說，第其年月，編為《唐年補錄》，凡六十五卷，識者賞之。
units.en: Besides literary composition, Wei was diligent in historical writing. Because the Veritable Records of the Tang emperors from Emperor Wuzong onward were missing, he collected recent hearsay and materials from various minor histories, arranged them chronologically, and compiled 《Supplement to the Annals of Tang》 in sixty-five volumes, which discerning readers praised.
units.literal: Apart from literary composition, Wei was diligent in writing. Because the Veritable Records of the Tang emperors from Emperor Wuzong downward were missing and unrecorded, he gathered recent hearsay and materials from various minor histories, arranged them by year and month, and compiled them as 《Supplement to the Annals of Tang》, sixty-five volumes in all, which discerning readers praised.

units.zh: 〈（《景文集》：緯博學善詞章，論議明銳，一時諸儒皆屈。
units.en: (From 《Collected Works of Jing》: Wei was broadly learned and skilled in letters; his arguments were sharp and clear, and the scholars of the day all yielded to him.
units.literal: (《Collected Works of Jing》: Wei was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition; his discourse was sharp and clear, and the scholars of the age all yielded to him.

units.zh: 唐自武宗後，史錄亡散，君掇拾殘余，為《唐年補錄》數十萬言，敘成敗事甚悉，書顯於時。）〉
units.en: After Emperor Wuzong of Tang, historical records were lost and scattered. Wei gathered the surviving fragments and produced 《Supplement to the Annals of Tang》 in several hundred thousand characters, narrating successes and failures in great detail, and the book won renown in its time.)〉
units.literal: After Emperor Wuzong of Tang, historical records were lost and scattered; the gentleman gathered the surviving fragments and produced 《Supplement to the Annals of Tang》 in several hundred thousand characters, narrating successes and failures in great detail, and the book was celebrated in its time.)〉

units.zh: 晉天福中，入為監察御史，改太常博士。
units.en: During the Tianfu era of Jin he entered court as Investigating Censor and was later transferred to Erudite of the Ministry of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he entered court as Investigating Censor, then was changed to Erudite of the Ministry of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 緯常以史才自負，銳於編述，不樂曲臺之任，乃陳情於相座。
units.en: Wei often prided himself on his talent for history and was eager to compile and write. Unhappy with his post at the Ministry of Imperial Sacrifices, he appealed to the chief minister.
units.literal: Wei often prided himself on his talent for history and was keen on compilation and writing; he did not relish his post at the Ministry of Imperial Sacrifices and therefore stated his wishes to the chief minister.

units.zh: 又與監修國史趙瑩詩曰：「滿朝唯我相，秉柄無親讎，三年司大董，最切是編修，史才不易得，勤勤處處求。
units.en: He also sent a poem to Zhao Ying, who supervised the compilation of the national history, saying, "In the whole court only I am minister; in holding power I have no personal enemy. For three years I have overseen the great commission, and what matters most is compilation. Talent for history is hard to find, and I seek it diligently everywhere.
units.literal: He also sent a poem to Zhao Ying, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, saying, "In the whole court only I am minister; holding power, I have no personal enemy. For three years I have overseen the great commission; what is most urgent is compilation. Talent for history is not easily found—I seek it diligently everywhere.

units.zh: 愚從年始立，東觀思優遊，昔時人未許，今來虛白頭，春臺與秋閣，往往興歸愁，信運北闕下，不系如虛舟。
units.en: I, slow-witted as I am, have dreamed since coming of age of leisurely work at the Eastern Pavilion. In former days men did not approve me, and now my white head has been wasted. The Spring Office and Autumn Office often stir thoughts of withdrawal in sorrow; truly my fate beneath the northern gate is unmoored, like an empty boat adrift.
units.literal: I, the dull one, since the year I came of age have thought of leisurely ease at the Eastern Pavilion; in former days men did not approve me, and now I have wasted my white head. The Spring Office and Autumn Office often stir thoughts of returning in sorrow; truly my fate under the northern gate is unmoored, like an empty boat.

units.zh: 綿蕝非所好，一日疑三秋，何當適所願，便如升瀛洲。」
units.en: The sacrificial mat is not what I love; one day feels like three autumns. When may I fulfill my wish and rise as if to ascend to Yingzhou?"
units.literal: The sacrificial mat is not what I love; one day feels like three autumns. When may I attain my wish and ascend as if to Yingzhou?

units.zh: 未幾，轉屯田員外郎，改起居郎、史館修撰。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works, then reassigned as Diarist and compiler in the History Office.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works, then changed to Diarist and compiler in the History Office.

units.zh: 又謂瑩曰：「《唐史》一百三十卷，止於代宗，已下十餘朝未有正史，請與同職修之。」
units.en: He also told Ying, "The 《History of Tang》 in one hundred thirty volumes stops at Emperor Daizong, and for more than ten reigns thereafter there is no standard history. I ask to join my colleagues in compiling one."
units.literal: He also said to Ying, "The 《History of Tang》 in one hundred thirty volumes stops at Emperor Daizong; for more than ten reigns below that there is no standard history. I ask to join my colleagues in compiling it."

units.zh: 瑩以其言上奏，晉祖然之，謂李崧曰：「賈緯欲修《唐史》，如何？」
units.en: Ying reported this to the throne. The Jin emperor approved and asked Li Song, "Jia Wei wishes to compile the 《History of Tang》—what do you think?"
units.literal: Ying reported his words to the throne; the Jin emperor approved and said to Li Song, "Jia Wei wishes to compile the 《History of Tang》—what do you think?"

units.zh: 對曰：「臣每見史官輩言，唐朝近百年來無實錄，既無根本，安能編紀。」
units.en: He replied, "Your subject often hears the historiographers say that for nearly a hundred years of the Tang there are no Veritable Records. Without a foundation, how can one compile a chronicle?"
units.literal: He replied, "Your subject often hears the historiographers say that for nearly a hundred years of Tang there are no Veritable Records; without a foundation, how can one compile and arrange a chronicle?"

units.zh: 緯聞崧言，頗怒，面責崧沮己。
units.en: When Wei heard Song's reply he grew angry and rebuked Song to his face for obstructing him.
units.literal: When Wei heard Song's words he grew quite angry and rebuked Song to his face for obstructing him.

units.zh: 崧曰：「與公鄉人，理須相惜，此事非細，安敢輕言。」
units.en: Song said, "I am your fellow townsman, and by rights we ought to look out for one another. This is no small matter—how dare I speak lightly?"
units.literal: Song said, "I am a fellow townsman of yours, and by right we ought to look out for one another. This matter is no small thing—how dare I speak lightly?"

units.zh: 緯與宰臣論說不已。
units.en: Wei continued arguing with the chief ministers without letup.
units.literal: Wei argued with the chief ministers without cease.

units.zh: 明年春，敕修《唐史》，緯在籍中。
units.en: The following spring an edict ordered the compilation of the 《History of Tang》, and Wei was listed among the compilers.
units.literal: The next spring an edict ordered the compilation of the 《History of Tang》, and Wei was listed among the compilers.

units.zh: 月餘，丁內艱，歸真定。
units.en: A little more than a month later he entered mourning for his mother and returned to Zhending.
units.literal: After a little more than a month he entered mourning for his mother and returned to Zhending.

units.zh: 開運初，服闋，復起居郎，修撰如故，尋以本官知制誥。
units.en: At the start of Kaiyun, when his mourning ended, he resumed his post as Diarist and continued as compiler as before. Soon he was given his existing office with concurrent duty drafting edicts.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, when mourning ended, he resumed his post as Diarist and continued as compiler as before; soon he was given his existing office with concurrent duty drafting edicts.

units.zh: 緯長於記註，應用文筆，未能過人，而議論剛強，儕類不平之，因目之為「賈鐵嘴」。
units.en: Wei was skilled at annals, notes, and practical writing, though he did not surpass others in those arts. His arguments, however, were forceful and unyielding, and his peers resented him, so they nicknamed him "Iron Mouth Jia."
units.literal: Wei was skilled at annals and notes and at practical writing, but did not surpass others; yet his discourse was forceful and unyielding, and his peers resented it, so they nicknamed him "Iron Mouth Jia."

units.zh: 開運中，累遷中書舍人。
units.en: During the Kaiyun era he was promoted in succession to Drafter in the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the Kaiyun era he was repeatedly promoted to Drafter in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 契丹入京師，隨契丹至真定，後與公卿還朝，授左諫議大夫。
units.en: When the Khitans entered the capital, he followed them to Zhending. Later he returned to court with the high officials and was appointed Left Remonstrance Adviser.
units.literal: When the Khitans entered the capital, he followed them to Zhending; afterward he returned to court with the high officials and was appointed Left Remonstrance Adviser.

units.zh: 緯以久次綸閣，比望丞郎之拜，及遷諫署，觖望彌甚。
units.en: Wei had long served in the drafting office and had hoped for appointment as a vice minister or director. When he was transferred instead to the remonstrance office, his disappointment grew all the sharper.
units.literal: Wei, having long served in the drafting office, had hoped for appointment as a vice minister or director; when he was moved to the remonstrance office instead, his disappointment grew all the sharper.

units.zh: 蘇逢吉監修國史，以緯頻投文字，甚知之，尋充史館修撰，判館事。
units.en: Su Fengji supervised the compilation of the national history. Because Wei frequently submitted writings, Su knew him well and soon appointed him compiler in the History Office with charge of its affairs.
units.literal: Su Fengji supervised the compilation of the national history; because Wei frequently submitted writings, he knew him well, and soon Wei was made compiler in the History Office and put in charge of its affairs.

units.zh: 乾祐中，受詔與王伸、竇儼修漢高祖實錄，緯以筆削為己任，然而褒貶之際，憎愛任情。
units.en: In the Qianyou era he received an edict to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozu of Han together with Wang Shen and Dou Yan. Wei took editorial judgment as his personal charge, yet in praise and blame he let personal likes and dislikes rule.
units.literal: In the Qianyou era he received an edict to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozu of Han together with Wang Shen and Dou Yan; Wei took the brush as his own charge, yet in praise and blame he let affection and hatred rule.

units.zh: 晉相桑維翰執政日，薄緯之為人，不甚見禮，緯深銜之。
units.en: While Jin chancellor Sang Weihan held power, he looked down on Wei's character and did not treat him with much courtesy, and Wei deeply resented it.
units.literal: In the days when Jin chancellor Sang Weihan held power, he looked down on Wei's character and did not treat him with much courtesy; Wei deeply resented it.

units.zh: 及敘《維翰傳》：「身沒之後，有白金八千鋌，他物稱是。」
units.en: When he came to write Sang Weihan's biography, he recorded, "After his death there were eight thousand ingots of white gold, with other goods in proportion."
units.literal: When he came to write the biography of Weihan, he wrote, "After his death there were eight thousand ingots of white gold, with other goods in proportion."

units.zh: 翰林學士徐臺符，緯邑人也，與緯相善，謂緯曰：「切聞吾友書桑魏公白金之數，不亦多乎！
units.en: Hanlin Academician Xu Taifu, a fellow townsman of Wei, was on good terms with him and said, "I have just heard, my friend, that you recorded the amount of white gold belonging to Duke Sang of Wei—is that not rather much!
units.literal: Hanlin Academician Xu Taifu, a fellow townsman of Wei, was on good terms with him and said to Wei, "I have just heard, my friend, that you wrote the amount of white gold belonging to Duke Sang of Wei—is it not rather much!

units.zh: 但以十目所睹，不可厚誣。」
units.en: But what many eyes have seen cannot be grossly misrepresented."
units.literal: But what ten eyes have seen cannot be grossly misrepresented."

units.zh: 緯不得已，改為白金數千錠。
units.en: Wei had no choice and changed the figure to several thousand ingots of white gold.
units.literal: Wei had no choice and changed it to several thousand ingots of white gold.

units.zh: 緯以撰述之勞，每詣宰執，懇祈遷轉，遇內難不果。
units.en: For his labors in composition, Wei often visited the chief ministers and earnestly sought transfer and promotion, but domestic mourning prevented it.
units.literal: For his labors in composition, Wei often visited the chief ministers and earnestly sought transfer and promotion, but when domestic mourning occurred it did not come to pass.

units.zh: 太祖即位，改給事中，判館如故。
units.en: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, Wei was made attendant gentleman and continued his concurrent duty directing the academy as before.
units.literal: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, Wei was made attendant gentleman and continued his concurrent duty as director of the academy as before.

units.zh: 先是，竇貞固奏請修晉朝實錄，既竟，亦望升擢。
units.en: Earlier, Dou Zhengu had memorialized to compile the Jin dynasty Veritable Records; when that was finished, he too hoped for promotion.
units.literal: Earlier, Dou Zhengu had memorialized requesting the compilation of Jin dynasty Veritable Records; when that was finished, he too hoped for promotion.

units.zh: 貞固猶在相位，乃上疏抗論除拜不平。
units.en: Zhengu was still chancellor, so Wei submitted a memorial arguing forcefully that appointments were unfair.
units.literal: Zhengu was still in the chancellorship, so Wei submitted a memorial arguing forcefully that appointments were unfair.

units.zh: 既而以所撰日曆示監修王峻，皆媒孽貞固及蘇禹珪之短，歷詆朝士之先達者。
units.en: He then showed the calendar he had compiled to supervising compiler Wang Jun; it all slandered the faults of Zhengu and Su Yugui and reviled senior court officials in turn.
units.literal: He then showed the calendar he had compiled to supervising compiler Wang Jun; it all slandered the faults of Zhengu and Su Yugui and reviled in turn the senior court officials.

units.zh: 峻惡之，謂同列曰：「賈給事家有士子，亦要門閥無玷，今滿朝並遭非毀，教士子何以進身！」
units.en: Jun resented this and said to his colleagues, "Attendant Gentleman Jia has a scholar-son at home and also values an unstained family name. Now the whole court is being slandered together—how can scholar-sons advance themselves!"
units.literal: Jun resented this and said to his colleagues, "Attendant Gentleman Jia has a scholar-son at home and also values a family name without stain. Now the whole court is being slandered together—how can scholar-sons advance themselves!"

units.zh: 乃於太祖前言之，出為平盧軍行軍司馬。
units.en: He then spoke of it before Emperor Taizu, and Wei was demoted to acting army marshal of the Pinglu Army.
units.literal: He then spoke of it before Emperor Taizu, and Wei was demoted to acting army marshal of the Pinglu Army.

units.zh: 時符彥卿鎮青州，以緯文士，厚禮之。
units.en: At the time Fu Yanqing was stationed at Qing Prefecture; regarding Wei as a literary gentleman, he treated him with great courtesy.
units.literal: At the time Fu Yanqing was stationed at Qing Prefecture; regarding Wei as a literary gentleman, he treated him with great courtesy.

units.zh: 緯妻以緯左遷，駭惋傷離，病留於京。
units.en: Because of Wei's demotion, his wife was alarmed and grieved at parting; she fell ill and remained in the capital.
units.literal: Wei's wife, because of his demotion, was alarmed and grieved at parting; she fell ill and remained in the capital.

units.zh: 緯書候之曰：「勉醫藥，來春與子同歸獲鹿。」
units.en: Wei wrote to inquire after her, saying, "Take medicine diligently; next spring I shall return with our son to Huolu."
units.literal: Wei wrote to inquire after her, saying, "Take medicine diligently; next spring I shall return with our son to Huolu."

units.zh: 廣順二年春，緯卒。
units.en: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, Wei died.
units.literal: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, Wei died.

units.zh: 及訃至，妻一慟而終，果雙柩北歸，聞者嘆之。
units.en: When the death notice arrived, his wife died in a single fit of grief; the two coffins were indeed borne north together, and those who heard of it sighed.
units.literal: When the death notice arrived, his wife died in a single fit of grief; indeed the two coffins were borne north together, and those who heard of it sighed.

units.zh: 緯有集三十卷，目曰《草堂集》，並聽撰《唐年補錄》六十五卷，皆傳於世。
units.en: Wei left a collection of writings in thirty juan entitled 《Record of the Thatched Hall》, and was also permitted to compile the 《Supplementary Record of Tang Years》 in sixty-five juan; both circulated in the world.
units.literal: Wei left a collection of writings in thirty juan entitled 《Record of the Thatched Hall》, and was also permitted to compile the 《Supplementary Record of Tang Years》 in sixty-five juan; both circulated in the world.

units.zh: 趙延乂，字子英，秦州人。
units.en: Zhao Yanyi, whose courtesy name was Ziying, was a native of Qin Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhao Yanyi, courtesy name Ziying, was a native of Qin Prefecture.

units.zh: 曾祖省躬，以明術數為通州司馬，遇亂避地於蜀。
units.en: His great-grandfather Shenggong, skilled in numerology and divination, served as Vice Prefect of Tong Prefecture. When disorder broke out he fled to Shu for refuge.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Shenggong, skilled in numerology and divination, served as Vice Prefect of Tong Prefecture; when disorder came he fled to Shu for refuge.

units.zh: 祖師古，黔中經略判官。
units.en: His grandfather Shigu served as administrative aide to the military commissioner of Qianzhong.
units.literal: His grandfather Shigu was administrative aide to the military commissioner of Qianzhong.

units.zh: 父溫珪，仕蜀為司天監。
units.en: His father Wengui served Shu as Director of the Astronomy Bureau.
units.literal: His father Wengui served Shu as Director of the Astronomy Bureau.

units.zh: 溫珪長於袁、許之術，兼之推步。
units.en: Wengui was skilled in the divinatory arts associated with Yuan Tian'gang and Xu Fu, and also in calendrical calculation.
units.literal: Wengui was skilled in the arts of Yuan and Xu, and also in calendrical calculation.

units.zh: 王建時，深蒙寵待，延問得失，事微差跌，即被詰讓。
units.en: Under Wang Jian he enjoyed deep favor. When consulted on success and failure, if anything went even slightly wrong he was immediately rebuked.
units.literal: Under Wang Jian he was deeply favored; when consulted on success and failure, if anything went even slightly wrong he was immediately rebuked.

units.zh: 臨終謂其子曰：「技術雖是世業，吾仕蜀已來，幾由技術而死，爾輩能以他途致身，亦良圖也。」
units.en: On his deathbed he told his sons, "Though technical arts are our family profession, since I entered service in Shu I have nearly died because of them. If you can establish yourselves by another path, that would be a wise course."
units.literal: On his deathbed he said to his sons, "Though technical arts are our family profession, since I entered service in Shu I have nearly died because of them. If you can establish yourselves by another path, that too is a good plan."

units.zh: 延乂少以家法仕蜀，由蔭為奉禮部翰林待詔。
units.en: Yanyi entered Shu service in youth through the family profession and, through hereditary privilege, became a Hanlin Awaiting Edict in the Ministry of Ceremonies.
units.literal: Yanyi in youth entered Shu service through the family profession; through hereditary privilege he became a Hanlin Awaiting Edict in the Ministry of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 蜀亡入洛，時年三十。
units.en: When Shu fell he went to Luoyang, at the age of thirty.
units.literal: When Shu fell he entered Luoyang, aged thirty.

units.zh: 天成中，得蜀舊職。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era he recovered his former post from Shu.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he recovered his former Shu post.

units.zh: 延乂世為星官，兼通三式，尤長於袁、許之鑒。
units.en: Yanyi came from generations of astral officials, was also versed in the Three Methods of divination, and was especially skilled in the discernment taught in the Yuan and Xu traditions.
units.literal: Yanyi came from generations of astral officials, was also versed in the Three Methods, and was especially skilled in the discernment of Yuan and Xu.

units.zh: 清泰中，嘗與樞密直學士呂琦同宿於內廷，琦因從容密問國家運祚，延乂曰：「來年厄會之期，俟過別論。」
units.en: During the Qingtai era he once lodged overnight in the inner court with Direct Academician of Military Affairs Lu Qi. Qi then casually asked in private about the dynasty's fortune, and Yanyi replied, "Next year is the term of calamity. Wait until it has passed and we may discuss the matter separately."
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he once lodged overnight in the inner court with Direct Academician of Military Affairs Lu Qi; Qi then, at ease, privately asked about the dynasty's fortune, and Yanyi said, "Next year is the term of calamity; wait until it has passed and we may discuss it separately."

units.zh: 琦訊之不已，延乂曰：「保邦在刑政，保祚在福德。
units.en: Qi pressed him without letup, and Yanyi said, "Preserving the state lies in penal administration; preserving the mandate lies in virtue and merit.
units.literal: Qi pressed him without cease, and Yanyi said, "Preserving the state lies in penal administration; preserving the mandate lies in virtue and merit.

units.zh: 在刑政則術士不敢言，奈際會諸公，罕有卓絕福德者，下官實有恤緯之僭。」
units.en: Where penal administration is concerned, diviners dare not speak plainly. Yet among the lords who meet at court, few possess outstanding virtue and merit, and your humble servant truly oversteps in worrying like a wife anxious for the state."
units.literal: Where penal administration is concerned, technicians dare not speak; yet among the lords who meet at court, few have outstanding virtue and merit, and your humble servant truly oversteps in worrying like a wife about the state's cords."

units.zh: 其年，兼衛尉少卿。
units.en: That year he was concurrently appointed Vice Minister of the Guard.
units.literal: That year he was concurrently appointed Vice Minister of the Guard.

units.zh: 晉天福中，代馬重績為司天監。
units.en: During the Tianfu era of Jin he replaced Ma Chongji as Director of the Astronomy Bureau.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he replaced Ma Chongji as Director of the Astronomy Bureau.

units.zh: 契丹入京師，隨至鎮州，時契丹滿達勒為帥，會漢高祖定兩京，控鶴都將李筠與諸校密謀劫庫兵，逐契丹，猶豫未決，謀於延乂，因假以術數贊成之。
units.en: When the Khitans entered the capital he followed them to Zhen Prefecture, where the Khitan Mandale was commander. When Emperor Gaozu of Han secured the Two Capitals, Li Jun, commander of the Crane-Controlled Army, and several officers secretly plotted to seize weapons from the armory and drive out the Khitans. Hesitating and unable to decide, they consulted Yanyi, who used divination to encourage them.
units.literal: When the Khitans entered the capital he followed them to Zhen Prefecture; at the time the Khitan Mandale was commander. When Emperor Gaozu of Han secured the Two Capitals, Li Jun, commander of the Crane-Controlled Army, and several officers secretly plotted to seize the armory weapons and drive out the Khitans; hesitating and unable to decide, they consulted Yanyi, and he lent them divination to encourage them.

units.zh: 契丹既去，還京師，官秩如舊。
units.en: After the Khitans departed he returned to the capital with his rank and office unchanged.
units.literal: After the Khitans departed he returned to the capital, and his rank and office were as before.

units.zh: 廣順初，加檢校司徒，本官如故，太祖數召對焉。
units.en: At the start of Guangshun he was given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor while retaining his original office, and Taizu repeatedly summoned him for audience.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and kept his original office; Taizu repeatedly summoned him for audience.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：周太祖自魏以兵入京師，召延乂問：「漢祚短促者，天數耶？」
units.en: (From 《History of the Five Dynasties by Ouyang》: Emperor Taizu of Zhou entered the capital from Wei at the head of an army and summoned Yanyi to ask, "Was the brevity of the Han mandate ordained by Heaven?"
units.literal: (《History of the Five Dynasties by Ouyang》: Emperor Taizu of Zhou entered the capital from Wei with troops and summoned Yanyi to ask, "Was the brevity of Han's mandate a matter of Heaven's number?"

units.zh: 延乂言：「王者撫天下，當以仁恩德澤，而漢淫酷，刑法枉濫，天下稱冤，此其所以亡也。」
units.en: Yanyi replied, "A ruler who pacifies the realm should do so through benevolence, grace, and virtue. Yet the Han was licentious and cruel, its penal laws perverse and excessive, and the realm cried out in grievance—that is why it perished."
units.literal: Yanyi said, "A king who pacifies the realm ought to do so through benevolence, grace, and virtue; yet Han was licentious and cruel, its penal laws perverse and excessive, and the realm cried out its grievance—this is why it perished."

units.zh: 是時太祖方以兵圍蘇逢吉、劉銖第，欲誅其族，聞延乂言悚然，因貸其族，二家獲全。）〉
units.en: At that time Taizu had troops besieging the residences of Su Fengji and Liu Zhu and intended to execute their entire clans. When he heard what Yanyi said he was startled, spared both clans, and the two families were saved.)〉
units.literal: At that time Taizu was just then leading troops in a siege of the residences of Su Fengji and Liu Zhu, intending to execute their entire clans; when he heard Yanyi's words he was startled, and therefore spared their clans, and both families were preserved.)〉

units.zh: 延乂善交遊，達機變，兼有技術，見者歡心。
units.en: Yanyi was skilled at making friends, quick to grasp shifting circumstances, and also possessed technical arts; everyone who met him took an immediate liking to him.
units.literal: Yanyi was skilled at forming friendships, understood adaptability and timely change, and also possessed technical arts; those who saw him delighted in him.

units.zh: 二年，授太府卿，判司天監事。
units.en: In the second year he was appointed Minister of the Grand Treasury and put in charge of the Astronomy Bureau.
units.literal: In the second year he was appointed Minister of the Grand Treasury and given concurrent charge of the Astronomy Bureau.

units.zh: 其年夏初，火犯靈臺，延乂自言星官所忌，又言身命宮災並，未幾其子卒，尋又妻卒，俄而延乂嬰疾，故人省之，舉手曰：「多謝諸親，死災不可逭也。」
units.en: At the beginning of that summer, Mars trespassed against the Observatory. Yanyi said this was an omen star officials dread, and that calamity was converging on his life palace. Before long his son died, then his wife, and soon Yanyi himself fell gravely ill. When old friends came to visit, he raised his hand and said, "My thanks to you all—the death I foresaw cannot be avoided."
units.literal: That summer at the year's beginning, fire trespassed against the Observatory; Yanyi himself said this was what star officials ought to dread, and also said calamity in his life palace was converging. Before long his son died; soon after his wife died; then in no time Yanyi himself fell gravely ill. When old friends came to visit him, he raised his hand and said, "Many thanks to you all, my kin—the calamity of death cannot be escaped."

units.zh: 尋卒，年五十八。
units.en: He died soon after, at the age of fifty-eight.
units.literal: Soon after he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

units.zh: 贈光祿卿。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 沈遘，字期遠，睢陽人也。
units.en: Shen Gou, whose courtesy name was Qiyuan, was a native of Suiyang.
units.literal: Shen Gou, courtesy name Qiyuan, was a native of Suiyang.

units.zh: 父振，貝州永濟令，累贈左諫議大夫。
units.en: His father Zhen served as magistrate of Yongji in Beizhou and was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Left Reminder of the Censorate.
units.literal: His father Zhen was magistrate of Yongji in Beizhou and was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Left Reminder of the Censorate.

units.zh: 遘幼孤，以苦學為誌，弱冠登進士第，釋褐除校書郎，由御史臺主簿拜監察御史，凡五遷至金部郎中，充三司判官。
units.en: Gou lost his father young and devoted himself to rigorous study. In his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as a collator, rose from chief clerk of the Censorate to investigating censor, and after five promotions reached Director of the Ministry of Revenue, where he served as judge of the Three Offices.
units.literal: Gou was orphaned young and took arduous study as his aim; in his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination, left office as collator, rose from chief clerk of the Censorate to investigating censor, and in five promotions reached Director of the Ministry of Revenue, serving as judge of the Three Offices.

units.zh: 廣順中，以本官知制誥。
units.en: During the Guangshun era he retained his existing rank and was appointed drafter of edicts.
units.literal: In the Guangshun era he held his former office and served as drafter of edicts.

units.zh: 世宗嗣位，擢為翰林院學士，歲滿，拜中書舍人充職。
units.en: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to academician of the Hanlin Academy. When his term was fulfilled he was appointed Secretariat Drafter in full capacity.
units.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to academician of the Hanlin Academy; when his term was complete he was appointed Secretariat Drafter in full capacity.

units.zh: 顯德三年夏，以扈從南征，因為遇疾歸，及京而卒。
units.en: In the summer of the third year of Xiande he accompanied the southern campaign as an imperial attendant, fell ill on the way home, and died after reaching the capital.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year of Xiande he accompanied the southern campaign as an attendant, then returned home because of illness, and died after reaching the capital.

units.zh: 遘為人謙和，勤於接下，每文士投贄，必擇其賢者而譽之，故當時後進之士多歸焉。
units.en: Gou was modest and gentle by nature and diligent in welcoming those beneath him. Whenever literary men submitted presentation pieces, he always singled out the worthy for praise, and many rising scholars of the day therefore gathered around him.
units.literal: Gou was modest and gentle by nature, diligent in receiving those below him; whenever literary men submitted presentation pieces, he always selected the worthy among them for praise, so younger scholars of the time mostly rallied to him.

units.zh: 李知損，字化機，大梁人也。
units.en: Li Zhisun, whose courtesy name was Huaji, was a native of Daliang.
units.literal: Li Zhisun, courtesy name Huaji, was a native of Daliang.

units.zh: 少輕薄，利口無行。
units.en: In his youth he was frivolous, sharp-tongued, and devoid of decent conduct.
units.literal: In youth he was frivolous, sharp-tongued, and without proper conduct.

units.zh: 梁朝時，以牒刺篇詠出入於內臣之門，繇是浪得虛譽，時人目之為「李羅隱」。
units.en: During the Liang dynasty he circulated occasional poems and verses through the doors of palace eunuchs and thereby won an empty reputation he did not deserve. People of the time nicknamed him "Li Luoyin," after the poet.
units.literal: In the Liang era he circulated occasional poems and verses through the doors of inner eunuchs, and thereby undeservedly gained empty reputation; people of the time styled him "Li Luoyin."

units.zh: 為累藩鎮從事，入拜左補闕，歷刑部兵二員外、度支判官、右司郎中。
units.en: He served in turn as staff officer to several military commissioners, entered the capital as Left Supplementation Officer, and held the posts of Vice Director of the Ministries of Justice and War, revenue judge, and Right Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He successively served as staff officer to several military commissioners, entered the capital as Left Supplementation Officer, and held the posts of Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, revenue judge, and Right Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 坐受榷鹽使王景遇厚賂，謫於均州。
units.en: He was demoted to Jun Prefecture for accepting heavy bribes from the salt monopoly commissioner Wang Jingyu.
units.literal: He was demoted to Jun Prefecture for accepting heavy bribes from the salt monopoly commissioner Wang Jingyu.

units.zh: 漢初歸朝，除右司郎中，兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: At the beginning of the Han dynasty he returned to court, was appointed Right Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
units.literal: At the beginning of Han he returned to court, was appointed Right Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

units.zh: 廣順中，拜右諫議大夫。
units.en: During the Guangshun era he was appointed Right Reminder of the Censorate.
units.literal: In the Guangshun era he was appointed Right Reminder of the Censorate.

units.zh: 時王峻為樞密使，知損以與峻有舊，遂指峻求使於江浙，峻為上言。
