units.en: At the time Wang Jun served as Commissioner of Military Affairs. Zhisun, who had old ties with Jun, asked Jun to recommend him as envoy to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and Jun put the request before the emperor.
units.literal: At the time Wang Jun was Commissioner of Military Affairs; Zhisun, because he had old ties with Jun, then pointed to Jun and requested appointment as envoy to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and Jun spoke on his behalf to the emperor.

units.zh: 太祖素聞知損所為，甚難之。
units.en: Taizu had long heard of Zhisun's conduct and was very reluctant to approve.
units.literal: Taizu had long heard of Zhisun's conduct and found the matter very difficult.

units.zh: 峻曰：「此人如或辱命，譴之可也。」
units.en: Jun said, "If this man disgraces his mission, he can be punished afterward."
units.literal: Jun said, "If this man should disgrace his mission, he can be punished afterward."

units.zh: 太祖重違其請，遂可之。
units.en: Taizu, reluctant to refuse Jun outright, approved the appointment.
units.literal: Taizu, unwilling heavily to refuse his request, thereupon assented.

units.zh: 知損既受命，大恣其荒誕之意，遂假資於人，廣備行李。
units.en: Once Zhisun received his commission, he indulged his wild and absurd impulses to the full, borrowing money from others and lavishly outfitting his baggage.
units.literal: Once Zhisun had received his commission, he fully indulged his wild and absurd inclinations, borrowing money from others and lavishly outfitting his baggage.

units.zh: 及即路，所經州郡，無不強貸，又移書於青州符彥卿，借錢百萬。
units.en: On the road, he forcibly borrowed money in every prefecture and commandery he passed, and also wrote to Fu Yanqing in Qing Prefecture requesting a loan of a million in cash.
units.literal: When he set out on the road, in every prefecture and commandery he passed he forcibly borrowed without exception, and also sent a letter to Fu Yanqing in Qing Prefecture asking to borrow a million in cash.

units.zh: 及在郵亭，行止穢雜。
units.en: At post stations his behavior was sordid and disgraceful.
units.literal: At post stations his comings and goings were sordid and disorderly.

units.zh: 王峻聞而奏之，乃責授棣州司馬。
units.en: When Wang Jun heard of it he reported him to the throne, and Zhisun was demoted to Military Adjutant of Di Prefecture.
units.literal: When Wang Jun heard of it he memorialized the throne, and Zhisun was demoted and appointed Military Adjutant of Di Prefecture.

units.zh: 世宗即位，切於求人，素聞知損狂狷，好上封事，謂有可采，且欲聞外事，即命征還，遽與復資。
units.en: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne he was eager to recruit talent. He had long heard that Zhisun was wild and outspoken and fond of submitting sealed memorials, believed some of his views worth adopting, and also wished to hear news from beyond the court. He at once ordered Zhisun recalled and quickly restored his rank.
units.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne he was eager to recruit men; he had long heard that Zhisun was wild and outspoken, fond of submitting sealed memorials, and believed there was material worth adopting; moreover he wished to hear of affairs beyond the court, and at once ordered him recalled and swiftly restored his rank.

units.zh: 數月之間，日貢章疏，多斥讟貴近，自謀進取，又上章求為過海使。
units.en: Within a few months he submitted memorials daily, many of them reviling powerful figures at court as he sought advancement for himself. He also submitted a memorial requesting appointment as envoy across the sea.
units.literal: Within a few months he daily submitted memorials, many reviling the great and the near, seeking advancement for himself; he also submitted a memorial requesting appointment as envoy across the sea.

units.zh: 世宗因發怒，仍以其醜行日彰，故命除名，配沙門島。
units.en: Emperor Shizong grew angry, and because Zhisun's disgraceful conduct was growing daily more conspicuous, ordered his name stricken from the rolls and sent him into exile on Shamen Island.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong thereupon grew angry; moreover because his disgraceful conduct grew daily more conspicuous, he ordered his name stricken from the rolls and sent him to exile on Shamen Island.

units.zh: 知損將行，謂所親曰：「余嘗遇善相者，言我三逐之後，當居相位，余自此而三矣，子姑待我。」
units.en: As Zhisun was about to depart he told those close to him, "I once met a skilled physiognomist who said that after three dismissals I would reach the chancellorship. This is my third—wait for me."
units.literal: As Zhisun was about to depart he said to those close to him, "I once met a skilled physiognomist who said that after three dismissals I would reach the chancellorship. I have now reached the third; wait for me a while."

units.zh: 後歲餘，卒於海中，其庸誕也如此。
units.en: A little over a year later he died at sea—such was the depth of his absurd presumption.
units.literal: More than a year later he died at sea—such was his absurd presumption.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：李知損，官至諫議大夫，好輕薄，時人謂之「李羅隱」。
units.en: (From 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Li Zhisun rose to Reminder of the Censorate. Fond of frivolity, he was known to his contemporaries as "Li Luoyin."
units.literal: (From 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Li Zhisun rose to Reminder of the Censorate. Fond of frivolity, he was known to his contemporaries as "Li Luoyin."

units.zh: 至於親友間往還簡牘，往往引裏巷常談，謂之偶對。
units.en: In letters exchanged among kin and friends he often drew on ordinary street talk, calling such passages "paired couplets."
units.literal: In letters exchanged among kin and friends he often cited common alley talk, calling such passages paired couplets.

units.zh: 常有朝士奉使回，以土物為贈，其意猶望卻回。
units.en: Once a court gentleman returning from an embassy gave him local products as a gift, apparently still hoping for a reciprocal gift in return.
units.literal: Once a court gentleman returning from an embassy offered him local products as a gift, still hoping for a return gift in exchange.

units.zh: 知損覺之，且貽書謝之曰：「在小子一時間卻擬送去，恐大官兩羅裏更不將來。」
units.en: Zhisun noticed this and wrote to thank him, saying, "For the moment this humble fellow was inclined to send it back—but I fear that you, a great official doubly styled 'Luoyin,' will never bring another."
units.literal: Zhisun noticed this and also sent a letter thanking him, saying, "For the moment this lesser fellow was inclined to send it back, but I fear that Your Excellency, doubly a 'Luoyin,' will never bring another."

units.zh: 乾祐中，奉使鄭州，時宋彥筠為節度。
units.en: During the Qianyou era he was sent on mission to Zheng Prefecture, when Song Yanyun was military commissioner.
units.literal: In the Qianyou era he was sent on mission to Zheng Prefecture, when Song Yanyun was military commissioner.

units.zh: 彥筠小字忙兒，因宴會，彥筠酒酣，輒問曰：「眾人何為號足下為羅隱？」
units.en: Yanyun's childhood name was Mang'er. At a banquet, when Yanyun was deep in his cups he asked repeatedly, "Why do people call you Luoyin?"
units.literal: Yanyun's childhood name was Mang'er; at a banquet, when Yanyun was deep in wine he repeatedly asked, "Why do people style you Luoyin?"

units.zh: 對曰：「下官平素好為詩，其格致大抵如羅隱，故人為號。」
units.en: Zhisun replied, "I have always loved writing poetry; its tone and spirit are much like Luoyin's, so my friends gave me the name."
units.literal: He replied, "This humble officer has always loved writing poetry; its style and spirit are generally like Luoyin's, so old friends gave me the name."

units.zh: 彥筠曰：「不然，蓋為足下輕薄如羅隱耳。」
units.en: Yanyun said, "Not so—it is because you are as frivolous as Luoyin."
units.literal: Yanyun said, "That is not so—it is because you are as frivolous as Luoyin."

units.zh: 知損大怒，厲聲曰：「只如令公，人皆謂之宋忙兒，未必便能放牛。」
units.en: Zhisun flew into a rage and said sharply, "Take Your Excellency, for instance—everyone calls you 'Busy Son Song,' but that hardly means you can actually herd cattle."
units.literal: Zhisun grew greatly angry and said in a harsh voice, "Take Your Excellency—for instance, everyone calls you 'Busy Son Song,' but that hardly means you can actually herd cattle."

units.zh: 滿座皆笑。）〉
units.en: The whole company burst out laughing.)〉
units.literal: The whole company burst out laughing.)〉

units.zh: 孫晟，本名鳳。
units.en: Sun Sheng—originally named Feng.
units.literal: Sun Sheng, original name Feng.

units.zh: 〈（《南唐書》云：孫忌，高密人，一名鳳，又名晟，少舉進士。）〉
units.en: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: Sun Ji was a native of Gaomi. He was also called Feng and also called Sheng, and in his youth he passed the jinshi examination.)〉
units.literal: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: Sun Ji was a native of Gaomi. He was also called Feng and also called Sheng, and in his youth he passed the jinshi examination.)〉

units.zh: 性陰賊，好奸謀。
units.en: By nature he was secretive and vicious, and fond of treacherous schemes.
units.literal: By nature he was secretive and vicious, fond of treacherous schemes.

units.zh: 少為道士，工詩，於廬山簡寂觀畫唐詩人賈島像，懸於屋壁，以禮事之。
units.en: In his youth he was a Daoist priest and skilled at poetry. At the Jianji Abbey on Mount Lu he painted a portrait of the Tang poet Jia Dao, hung it on the wall, and treated it with ritual reverence.
units.literal: In youth he was a Daoist priest, skilled at poetry; at the Jianji Abbey on Mount Lu he painted a portrait of the Tang poet Jia Dao and hung it on the wall, honoring it with ritual observance.

units.zh: 觀主以為妖妄，執杖驅出之，大為時輩所嗤。
units.en: The abbot judged this deluded and drove him out with a staff. His contemporaries mocked him roundly.
units.literal: The abbot regarded this as deluded and bizarre, took a staff and drove him out; he was greatly mocked by contemporaries.

units.zh: 改儒服，謁唐莊宗於鎮州，授秘書省著作郎。
units.en: He put on Confucian dress, presented himself to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang at Zhen Prefecture, and was appointed Compiler in the Secretariat.
units.literal: He changed to Confucian dress, presented himself to Tang Emperor Zhuangzong at Zhen Prefecture, and was appointed Compiler in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 〈（《南唐書》云：豆盧革為相，雅知忌，辟為判官。）〉
units.en: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: When Doulu Ge became chancellor he knew Ji well by reputation and recruited him as administrative aide.)〉
units.literal: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: When Doulu Ge became chancellor he knew Ji well by reputation and recruited him as administrative aide.)〉

units.zh: 天成初，朱守殷據夷門叛，時晟為幕賓，贊成其事。
units.en: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era Zhu Shouyin rebelled and held Yimen. Sheng was then a staff adviser and supported the rebellion.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Zhu Shouyin held Yimen in rebellion; at the time Sheng was a staff adviser and supported the affair.

units.zh: 是時晟常擐甲露刃，以十數騎自隨，巡行於市，多所屠害，汴人為之切齒。
units.en: At that time Sheng often wore armor with bared blade, keeping a dozen or so horsemen with him as he patrolled the markets and slaughtered many. The people of Bian gnashed their teeth at the mention of him.
units.literal: At that time Sheng often donned armor and bared his blade, keeping a dozen or so horsemen about him; he patrolled the markets and slaughtered many. The people of Bian gnashed their teeth over him.

units.zh: 城陷，朱氏被誅，晟乃匿跡更名，棄其妻子，亡命於陳、宋間。
units.en: When the city fell Zhu was executed. Sheng then went into hiding, changed his name, abandoned his wife and children, and fled for his life between Chen and Song.
units.literal: When the city fell Zhu was executed; Sheng then hid his tracks, changed his name, abandoned wife and children, and fled for his life between Chen and Song.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：安重誨惡晟，以為教守殷反者晟也，畫其像購之，不可得，遂族其家。
units.en: (From 《History of the Five Dynasties by Ouyang》: An Chonghui hated Sheng and believed Sheng had taught Zhu Shouyin to rebel. He posted Sheng's likeness with a reward offer but could not capture him, and therefore exterminated his clan.
units.literal: (From 《History of the Five Dynasties by Ouyang》: An Chonghui hated Sheng and believed Sheng had taught Zhu Shouyin to rebel. He posted Sheng's likeness with a reward offer but could not capture him, and therefore exterminated his clan.

units.zh: 晟奔於吳。）〉
units.en: Sheng fled to Wu.)〉
units.literal: Sheng fled to Wu.)〉

units.zh: 會同惡者送之過淮，吳人方納叛亡，即以偽官授之。
units.en: Men who likewise despised him escorted him across the Huai. The Wu were then accepting defectors and fugitives and at once granted him office in their puppet regime.
units.literal: Those who likewise hated him escorted him across the Huai; the Wu side was then accepting defectors and fugitives, and at once granted him an office in the puppet regime.

units.zh: 晟亦微有詞翰，李昇偽尊楊溥為讓皇之冊文，即晟之詞也，故江南尤重之。
units.en: Sheng also had some literary talent. The patent of honor in which Li Bian of the puppet regime elevated Yang Pu as abdicated emperor was written in Sheng's words, and Jiangnan therefore held him in particular esteem.
units.literal: Sheng also had some skill in literary composition; the patent of honor by which Li Bian in the puppet regime elevated Yang Pu as Emperor of Abdication was Sheng's wording, so Jiangnan especially valued him.

units.zh: 二十年間，累歷偽任，財貨邸第，頗適其意。
units.en: Over twenty years he rose through successive appointments in the puppet regime, accumulating wealth, goods, and a mansion that quite suited his wishes.
units.literal: Over twenty years he rose through successive puppet appointments; wealth, goods, and mansion all quite suited his wishes.

units.zh: 晟以家妓甚眾，每食不設食機，令眾妓各執一食器，周侍於其側，謂之「肉臺盤」，其自養稱愜也如是。
units.en: Sheng kept a great many household singing girls. At each meal he dispensed with a proper food table and had the girls each hold a food vessel and stand in attendance at his side—he called this a "flesh serving tray." Such was the life of indulgence that contented him.
units.literal: Because Sheng had very many household singing girls, at each meal he would not set out a food table but had the many girls each hold a food vessel and wait in attendance at his sides, calling this "flesh serving trays"—such was the way he pampered himself to satisfaction.

units.zh: 〈（《南唐書》云：忌為舒州節度使，治軍嚴，有歸化卒二人，正晝挺白刃入府，求忌殺之。
units.en: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: When Ji served as military commissioner of Shu Prefecture he governed the army strictly. Two surrendered soldiers drew bare blades in broad daylight, entered headquarters, and sought to kill him.
units.literal: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: When Ji served as military commissioner of Shu Prefecture he governed the army strictly. Two surrendered soldiers drew bare blades in broad daylight, entered headquarters, and sought to kill him.

units.zh: 入自西門，吏士倉卒莫能禦。
units.en: They entered by the west gate, and in the sudden crisis officials and soldiers could not stop them.
units.literal: They entered by the west gate; officials and soldiers in the sudden crisis could not resist.

units.zh: 適忌閑行在東門，聞亂，得民家馬乘之，奔桐城。
units.en: Ji happened to be strolling at the east gate. Hearing the disturbance, he borrowed a horse from a commoner's household, mounted it, and fled to Tongcheng.
units.literal: Just then Ji was strolling at the east gate; hearing the disturbance, he obtained a horse from a commoner's household, mounted it, and fled to Tongcheng.

units.zh: 叛卒不得忌，乃殺都押衙李建崇而逸。
units.en: The mutinous soldiers failed to catch Ji, killed the chief judge-adjutant Li Jianchong instead, and fled.
units.literal: The mutinous soldiers could not get Ji and so killed the chief judge-adjutant Li Jianchong and escaped.

units.zh: 忌坐貶光祿卿。）〉
units.en: Ji was demoted to Minister of Splendid Happiness.)〉
units.literal: Ji was demoted to Minister of Splendid Happiness for the offense.)〉

units.zh: 顯德三年春，王師下廣陵，江左驚窘，李景偽署晟為司空，令奉貢於行在，世宗遣右常侍劉悅伴之，賜與甚厚。
units.en: In the spring of the third year of Xiande the imperial army took Guangling and the Jiang left was thrown into alarm. Li Jing of the puppet regime appointed Sheng Minister of Works and ordered him to present tribute at the imperial camp. Emperor Shizong sent Right Regular Attendant Liu Yue to accompany him and lavished generous rewards upon him.
units.literal: In the spring of the third year of Xiande the imperial army descended on Guangling; the Jiang left was alarmed and distressed. Li Jing in the puppet regime appointed Sheng Minister of Works and ordered him to present tribute at the imperial camp; Emperor Shizong sent Right Regular Attendant Liu Yue to accompany him and bestowed rewards very generously.

units.zh: 洎隨駕到闕，舍於都亭驛，禮遇殊優。
units.en: When he followed the imperial procession to the capital he lodged at the Capital Pavilion Station, where he was treated with exceptional courtesy.
units.literal: When he followed the imperial procession to the capital he lodged at the Capital Pavilion Station; courtesies were exceptionally fine.

units.zh: 每召見，飲之醇醴，問以江南事，晟但言：「吳畏陛下之神武，唯以北面為求，保無二也。」
units.en: Whenever he was summoned he was given strong wine and questioned about affairs in Jiangnan. Sheng would say only, "Wu fears Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and seeks only to submit as your vassal facing north, guaranteeing there will be no second thought."
units.literal: Whenever he was summoned for audience they gave him strong wine and questioned him about Jiangnan affairs; Sheng only said, "Wu fears Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and seeks only to face north as a subject, guaranteeing there will be no second thought."

units.zh: 先是，張永德守下蔡，素與李重進不協，每宴將校，多暴其短。
units.en: Earlier Zhang Yongde held Xia Cai and had long been at odds with Li Chongjin. Whenever he feasted his officers he often aired Chongjin's faults.
units.literal: Earlier, Zhang Yongde held Xia Cai and had long been on bad terms with Li Chongjin; whenever he feasted his officers he often exposed Chongjin's faults.

units.zh: 一日，永德乘醉，乃大言重進潛蓄奸謀，當時將校無不驚駭，繇是人情大擾。
units.en: One day, while drunk, Yongde loudly declared that Chongjin was secretly plotting treason. The officers were all shocked, and morale was badly shaken.
units.literal: One day Yongde, taking advantage of drunkenness, then loudly declared that Chongjin secretly harbored treacherous designs; at the time the officers were all alarmed and terrified, and from this human sentiment was greatly disturbed.

units.zh: 後密遣親信乘驛上言，世宗不聽，亦不介意。
units.en: Later he secretly sent a trusted agent by express relay to report to the throne, but Emperor Shizong paid no heed and was unconcerned.
units.literal: Later he secretly sent a trusted man by express relay to memorialize the throne; Emperor Shizong did not listen and was not concerned.

units.zh: 一日，重進自壽陽去其部從，直指永德帳下，宴飲終日而去，自此人情稍安。
units.en: One day Chongjin left his escort at Shouyang and went straight to Yongde's headquarters, where they feasted all day before he departed. From then on morale gradually settled.
units.literal: One day Chongjin left his escort at Shouyang and went straight to Yongde's headquarters; they feasted and drank all day before he departed—from this human sentiment gradually grew calm.

units.zh: 時李景覘而知之，因密令人賫蠟書遺重進，勸為不軌，重進以其蠟書進呈，世宗覽之，皆斥讟反間之言。
units.en: Li Jing learned of this and secretly sent a man bearing a wax-sealed letter to Chongjin urging him to rebel. Chongjin presented the letter to the throne. Emperor Shizong read it and found it full of slander and words meant to sow discord.
units.literal: At the time Li Jing observed this and knew of it; he therefore secretly sent a man bearing a wax-sealed letter to Chongjin urging treason. Chongjin presented the wax letter to the throne; Emperor Shizong read it—all were words sowing discord and subversion.

units.zh: 世宗怒晟前言失實，因急召侍衛都虞候韓通令收晟下獄，與其從者百餘人皆誅之。
units.en: Emperor Shizong, angry that Sheng's earlier statements had been false, urgently summoned Palace Guard Director of Ceremonial Han Tong and ordered Sheng imprisoned. More than a hundred of his followers were executed as well.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong was angry that Sheng's earlier statements had been false, and therefore urgently summoned Palace Guard Director of Ceremonial Han Tong and ordered Sheng taken into prison; more than a hundred of his followers were also executed.

units.zh: 〈（《南唐書》云：世宗命都承旨曹翰護至右軍巡院，猶飲之酒，數酌，翰起曰：「相公得罪，賜自盡。」
units.en: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: Emperor Shizong ordered Chief Palatial Drafter Cao Han to escort him to the Right Army Circuit Court. They still gave him wine, and after several cups Han rose and said, "Lord Chancellor, you have offended and are granted the privilege of taking your own life."
units.literal: (From 《Book of Southern Tang》: Emperor Shizong ordered Chief Palatial Drafter Cao Han to escort him to the Right Army Circuit Court. They still gave him wine, and after several cups Han rose and said, "Lord Chancellor, you have offended and are granted the privilege of taking your own life."

units.zh: 忌怡然整衣索笏，東南望再拜曰：「臣受恩深，謹以死謝。」
units.en: Ji composed himself calmly, straightened his robes, took up his tablet, bowed twice toward the southeast, and said, "Your subject has received deep grace and accepts death in gratitude."
units.literal: Ji composed himself calmly, straightened his robe and sought his tablet, bowed twice toward the southeast and said, "Your subject has received deep grace and respectfully takes death in gratitude."

units.zh: 從者二百人，亦皆誅死於東相國寺。）〉
units.en: Two hundred followers were also executed at East Xiangguo Temple.)〉
units.literal: Two hundred followers were also all executed at East Xiangguo Temple.)〉

units.zh: 翌日，宰臣上謁，世宗親諭之，始知其事實。
units.en: The next day, when the chief ministers came to audience, Emperor Shizong personally explained the matter to them—and only then did they learn what had actually happened.
units.literal: The next day when the chief ministers came to audience, Emperor Shizong personally explained the matter to them, and only then did they learn the truth of the affair.

units.zh: 議者以晟昔構禍於梁民，令伏法於梁獄，報應之道，豈徒然哉！
units.en: Commentators observed that Sheng had once brought calamity upon the people of Liang and now met the law's punishment in a Liang prison—the way of retribution, they said, was hardly empty.
units.literal: Commentators held that since Sheng had once brought calamity upon the people of Liang, for him now to die by law in Liang's prison—was the way of retribution merely empty?

units.zh: 晟性慷慨，常感李景之厚遇，誓死以報之。
units.en: Sheng was generous by nature and deeply moved by Li Jing's generous treatment of him; he swore to repay that kindness with his life.
units.literal: Sheng was generous by nature and often felt deeply Li Jing's generous treatment of him, swearing to repay it with his death.

units.zh: 〈（《釣磯立談》云：晟將命周朝，自知不免，私謂副使王崇質曰：「吾思之熟矣，終不忍負永陵一壞土，余非所知也。」）〉
units.en: (From 《Collected Conversations from the Angler's Reef》: When Sheng was about to receive his commission to the Zhou court he knew he would not escape. He privately told Vice Envoy Wang Chongzhi, "I have thought this through carefully. In the end I cannot bear to betray even a clod of Yongling's soil—as for the rest, that is beyond what you can know.")〉
units.literal: (From 《Collected Conversations from the Angler's Reef》: When Sheng was about to receive his commission to the Zhou court he knew he would not escape. He privately told Vice Envoy Wang Chongzhi, "I have thought this through carefully. In the end I cannot bear to betray even a clod of Yongling's soil—as for the rest, that is beyond what you can know.")〉

units.zh: 及將下獄，世宗令近臣問以江南可取之狀，晟默然不對。
units.en: When he was about to be imprisoned Emperor Shizong had a close attendant ask him how Jiangnan might be taken. Sheng remained silent and would not answer.
units.literal: When he was about to be imprisoned Emperor Shizong ordered a close attendant to question him on how Jiangnan might be taken; Sheng was silent and did not answer.

units.zh: 臨刑之際，整其衣冠，南望金陵再拜而言曰：「臣惟以死謝。」
units.en: At the moment of execution he straightened his hat and robes, bowed twice toward Jinling in the south, and said, "Your subject can repay only with my death."
units.literal: At the moment of execution he straightened his hat and robes, bowed twice toward Jinling to the south and said, "Your subject can only repay with death."

units.zh: 遂伏誅。
units.en: He was then executed.
units.literal: Thereupon he was executed.
